## Bug-Introducing Commits
BIC: a5bc187faecd275117371622b048a8aa41a157cd

## Reasoning

**(1) Investigation:** I ran `git blame` on the lines touched by the fix commit (`editThemePage.waitUntilPreviewIsLoaded()` and `editThemePage = new EditThemePage()`), using the parent of the fix commit as the reference. This pinpointed commit `a5bc187faec` ("Simon Urli", 2019-11-20) as the commit that last touched those exact lines.

**(2) The bug:** I then viewed the full diff of `a5bc187faec`. It added a try/catch block to retry loading the theme preview on timeout, but referenced the wrong local variable. Just before this change, the code had:
```java
ViewThemePage themePage = themeApplicationWebHomePage.seeTheme(testMethodName);
themePage.waitUntilPreviewIsLoaded();
```
The commit replaced the correct `themePage.waitUntilPreviewIsLoaded()` call with `editThemePage.waitUntilPreviewIsLoaded()` and, in the catch block, reassigned `editThemePage = new EditThemePage();`. This `editThemePage` variable is an unrelated field from elsewhere in the test method (used earlier for the editing workflow) — not the `themePage` (a `ViewThemePage`) just created on the prior line. This causes the retry logic to operate on a stale/wrong page object instead of the view page that was just navigated to.

**(3) Evidence:** The fix commit `a154148c09` simply restores the correct variable usage — changing `editThemePage.waitUntilPreviewIsLoaded()` back to `themePage.waitUntilPreviewIsLoaded()` and `editThemePage = new EditThemePage()` back to `themePage = new ViewThemePage()` — an exact reversal of the erroneous substitution made in `a5bc187faec`. The diff in `a5bc187faec` is the sole place where this variable mix-up was introduced; no other commit in the file's history touches these lines until the fix.

I'm confident in this identification since the fix is a precise, line-level reversal of the change made in `a5bc187faec`.
